Dining at Dar Yacout was one of the highlights of our time in Marrakech. From the moment we walked through the doors, it felt like stepping into another era.  We began the evening with drinks on the beautiful rooftop while traditional Gnawa musicians performed, creating a wonderful atmosphere as the sun set over the Medina. The restaurant itself is stunning, with elegant courtyards, candlelit dining rooms, intricate Moroccan architecture, and countless beautiful details around every corner.  The service was absolutely stellar. Every member of the staff was attentive, welcoming, and made us feel like honored guests throughout the evening. Their hospitality elevated what was already a memorable experience.  Dinner was a multi-course traditional Moroccan feast featuring a variety of local specialties. Come hungry—there is plenty of food! While we enjoyed the meal, the ambiance, music, and exceptional service were the true stars of the evening.  What makes Dar Yacout so special is that it feels like much more than a restaurant. It's a cultural experience that combines history, architecture, music, outstanding hospitality, and Moroccan tradition into one unforgettable night.  If you're looking for a truly memorable evening in Marrakech, Dar Yacout is an experience not to be missed.
Spectacular experience: a great sampling of Moroccan food, a fantastic ambiance, and memories that will last a lifetime.

The location is beautiful, but everything about the dining experience was poorly handled and disappointing.  We were only informed once seated that there was a fixed menu, which should have been made clear beforehand. After the appetisers, we waited over an hour for the next course with no proper communication or updates. We were originally told we would be served lemon chicken tagine, but instead a large fried pigeon pie was brought out without warning. We were simply told there had been a problem in the kitchen, but nobody bothered to inform us during the long wait.  The food itself was neither luxurious nor refined. It felt heavy, basic, and focused on huge quantities rather than quality. The portions were excessively large, far more than reasonable for a family of four, and a significant amount went to waste.  Service was disorganised throughout. After the delay, we were moved straight to the next course with no real explanation or effort to manage the situation properly.  Water service was also handled unprofessionally: bottles were continuously opened and poured without asking, and we were later charged for every single one.  To make matters worse, we were told that the prices had been adjusted due to the inconvenience, but this was not reflected in the final bill. In the end, we paid far more than expected for a meal that was poorly communicated, poorly executed, and not worth the price.  A beautiful setting completely undermined by disorganised service, low-quality food, excessive portions, and a lack of basic professionalism. Not recommended.

Dar Yacout is undeniably stunning. The architecture, the rooftop views over the medina, the candlelit courtyards — visually, it's everything you'd hope for from a romantic evening in Marrakech. Unfortunately, the beauty of the place is where the praise ends.  The service was disorganized and frankly poor. We waited over an hour for our first course, and when it finally arrived it wasn't the lemon chicken we were expecting but pigeon with cinnamon and sugar — served without any warning that the menu had changed from what we'd anticipated. Throughout the meal, staff kept refilling our water without ever asking whether we wanted more, which felt less like attentiveness and more like a lack of basic communication.  The set menu itself was underwhelming and far less refined than the setting suggests. Portions were enormous — to the point of genuine waste, as plate after plate of barely-touched food was cleared away. The dessert, which should have been a high note, was equally disappointing.  To their credit, once we explained we couldn't eat the pigeon dish we hadn't been told about, they reduced our bill by 20 euros per person. But that gesture doesn't begin to make up for the rest. We paid over 300 euros for four people — one dish short, after more than an hour of waiting, for food that was genuinely basic and that we ended up leaving on our plates. A menu changed without a word of notice, and a meal that left us frustrated rather than delighted. It was, quite honestly, shameful.  There's a clear attempt here to present something sophisticated, but the execution simply doesn't match the ambition. A gorgeous venue can't compensate for slow, careless service and forgettable food. Sadly, not worth the visit.

Dar Yacout — A Majestic Moroccan Journey From the moment you emerge from the winding alleys of Marrakech’s medina and step through the imposing doors of Dar Yacout, you know you’ve crossed into another world—rich, intimate, and profoundly theatrical. A towering “genie” figure greets you at the entrance, a presence that feels both intimidating and welcoming, signaling that something extraordinary awaits inside. You’re guided through candlelit passages into a palatial riad, where every arch, mosaic, and carved plaster detail whispers stories of Moroccan artistry. At the center, a shimmering pool anchors the courtyard, lantern light dancing across its surface. The atmosphere is heightened by the haunting melodies of live Berber music (Gnaoua), setting the stage for an experience that feels timeless and transportive. The evening begins on the rooftop terrace, where cocktails are served, offering sweeping views of the medina and the distant Atlas Mountains. With music in the background and the city unfolding before you, it’s a perfect overture to the feast ahead. Dinner follows as a prix-fixe journey through Moroccan flavors. A spread of cold cooked salads arrives first—vibrant, colorful, and diverse in taste and texture. Then come the main courses: a fragrant chicken tagine, tender lamb couscous, and finally, a crisp pastry dessert drizzled with honey and sprinkled with nuts. The finale, of course, is the traditional mint tea accompanied by multi-layered tower trays of traditional Moroccan cookies, served with care and ceremony. The settings and service might almost distract from the food that may not be as impressive as the decor, but the way it’s presented makes the experience unforgettable. Service here is a performance in itself. A lead server, assisted by two attendants, orchestrates the progression of courses with flair and precision, turning the act of dining into something ceremonial. Every detail, from presentation to pacing, contributes to the sense of theater. Even the bathrooms deserve a mention—lavish and beautifully designed to match the grandeur of the palace. For two people, we spent approximately €240, which included the prix fixe dinner, a local bottle of very nice wine, water, and tips. Given the setting, entertainment, and level of service, the price felt reasonable in relation to the overall experience, but rather high compared to other dining options in Marrakesh. As the evening draws to a close, the doorman advises against walking through the maze of alleys at night. Ignoring his warning, we ventured out anyway and quickly found ourselves navigating the typical chaos of Marrakech—guided by persistent locals who demanded payment for showing us the way out. It was a jarring contrast to the serene magic inside, and a reminder of just how special the world of Dar Yacout really is. Why Dar Yacout Stands Out: Ambience & Décor: Palatial, theatrical, and utterly Moroccan—every detail immerses you in another era. Culinary Journey: A fixed-menu feast highlighting Moroccan cold salads, tagines, couscous, pastries, and mint tea. Service as Spectacle: Graceful, attentive, and orchestrated like a performance. View & Music: Rooftop cocktails paired with live Berber music and sweeping city views. Value: Around €240 for two, including wine, water, and tips—a fair price for such an immersive evening. Final Take: Dar Yacout is far more than a restaurant—it’s an experience. The architecture, setting, ceremonial service, and cultural immersion combine to create a night that feels like stepping into a Moroccan fairytale. While the food itself could be stronger in places, the overall journey makes this one of Marrakech’s most unforgettable dining experiences. One of the restaurants we visited during our trip was located within a residential neighborhood, which provided a unique and enriching perspective of local life. The atmosphere was pleasant, and the set menu included a generous succession of courses: appetizers, a main dish featuring chicken with couscous, followed by lamb, and for dessert, mint tea accompanied by a crisp, mille-feuille-style pastry.  While the setting and concept were interesting, we were quite struck by the excessive amount of food served. Several dishes remained completely untouched, not due to lack of quality, but simply because the quantity was far beyond what anyone could reasonably consume.  As is customary in our travels, I requested that the untouched portions be packed to share with our guide and driver, who were with us daily and treated us with great care and professionalism. I also considered offering the food to local residents, especially given the restaurant’s location within the community. Unfortunately, the restaurant manager was extremely impolite and firmly refused to wrap any leftovers, which I found quite disappointing and wasteful.  It was the only regrettable aspect of an otherwise exceptional and beautifully organized journey.

Dar Yacout in Marrakesh is truly a culinary gem that offers an unforgettable dining experience Nestled in the heart of the medina, this restaurant is renowned for its exquisite Moroccan cuisine and stunning traditional architecture. As you step inside, you're greeted by an opulent setting with intricate tile work, ornate wood carvings, and lush courtyards that transport you to a bygone era. The ambiance is nothing short of magical, with dimly lit lanterns casting a warm glow over the beautifully set tables. The menu is a celebration of Moroccan flavors, featuring classic dishes like tagines, couscous, and pastillas, all prepared with the freshest ingredients and a modern twist. Each dish is a masterpiece, bursting with aromatic spices and rich flavors that tantalize the taste buds. The service at Dar Yacout is impeccable, with attentive staff ensuring that every aspect of your meal is perfect. To top it all off, the restaurant offers breathtaking views of the city from its rooftop terrace, making it an ideal spot for a romantic dinner or a special celebration. Dining at Dar Yacout is not just a meal; it's an immersive cultural experience that captures the essence of Marrakesh in the most delightful way. Recommended dishes: Moroccan Salads, Couscous with Vegetables, Milk Pastilla, Pollo, Tagine De Ternera Makfoul

Dar Yacout  Country: Morocco.  Location: 79 Derb Sidi Ahmed Soussi, Bab Doukkala, Marrakech.  Cooking Style: Traditional Moroccan fine dining  Go There For:  • An immersive Moroccan dining experience in a stunning palace-like setting.  • Lavish multi-course meals featuring iconic Moroccan dishes prepared with exceptional finesse.  • A magical, candlelit rooftop terrace offering breathtaking views of Marrakech’s Medina.  • Unparalleled hospitality in an atmosphere of luxury and tradition.  What to Eat and What to Drink:  What to Eat:.  Dar Yacout offers a set menu that captures the essence of Moroccan cuisine with bold flavors and exceptional presentation. Highlights include:  • Starters: A generous spread of traditional Moroccan salads, including zaalouk (eggplant), taktouka (pepper and tomato), and carrot with cumin.  • Mains:  • Signature lamb tagine with prunes, almonds, and cinnamon, a masterpiece of balance between sweet and savory.  • Chicken pastilla, a rich, flaky pie filled with spiced chicken, almonds, and a dusting of powdered sugar and cinnamon.  • Desserts: Seasonal fresh fruits and traditional Moroccan pastries like gazelle horns, paired with mint tea.  What to Drink:  • Pair your meal with Moroccan wines, such as a crisp white from Meknes or a full-bodied red from the Atlas Mountains.  • The meal concludes with a must-try traditional mint tea, served theatrically in ornate silver teapots.  Chef and Philosophy:  Chef: The culinary team at Dar Yacout operates under the guidance of Moroccan culinary experts, committed to preserving traditional recipes and techniques.  Philosophy:.  Dar Yacout is dedicated to showcasing the depth and richness of Moroccan cuisine. The focus is on authentic flavors and textures, crafted from fresh, local ingredients. Dining here is a celebration of Morocco’s culinary heritage in a setting that reflects the grandeur of its culture.  Highlights from Critics:  • Michelin Green Guide: “A must-visit in Marrakech for anyone seeking a quintessential Moroccan dining experience.”  • Condé Nast Traveller: “An opulent setting and a feast fit for royalty.”  • Food bloggers: Praise the lamb tagine as one of the finest in Marrakech and the overall ambiance as “otherworldly.”  Signature Dishes:  • Lamb tagine with prunes and almonds  • Chicken pastilla  • Moroccan mezze of seasonal salads  • Traditional pastries with mint tea  Ratings and Reviews:  Overall Score: 88/100  Kitchen Score: 90/100  • Ingredients & Products: 92/100 – Fresh, local, and true to Moroccan tradition.  • Technique & Execution: 90/100 – Expertly crafted dishes that respect authenticity.  • Presentation: 88/100 – Simple yet elegant, enhancing the traditional aesthetic.  Wine List Score: 80/100  • A curated selection of Moroccan wines, offering good representation of local terroirs.  • Recommendations include Guerrouane Blanc or a red from Domaine de Sahari.  Ambiance Score: 98/100  • A breathtaking, palace-like setting with traditional Moroccan décor: intricate zellige tiles, carved plaster, and rich textiles.  • The rooftop terrace, with its views of Marrakech and its candlelit tables, is a highlight.  Service Score: 85/100  • Warm, attentive staff offering true Moroccan hospitality.  • Meals are served with grace and in a traditional, unhurried style. With a focus on preserving the authenticity of Moroccan cuisine while elevating it to fine dining, this is a must-visit destination for anyone seeking a true taste of Morocco in a setting fit for royalty.

Quite simply the most beautiful restaurant I have even been in, let alone eaten at. Here is the thing - it might seem like it’s ’just for tourists’ because Moroccans don’t traditionally go out for Moroccan food - they have it at home. But if you want to feel like you are going to someone’s beautiful home this is the place to go. The service is unparalleled, from the moment you walk in - greeted by all smiles at the entrance to where you are seated for a drink and greeted by more friendly faces. Prepare yourself and come hungry and with no timeline in mind because unlike other places that rush you out the door for their next table, you will be here for literally hours. The food starts to arrive with delicious renditions of traditional Moroccan salads and then a beautiful tagine and then and then and then - you will roll out of the place belly full and very happy. All the while you are serenaded by perfect music - it’s magical and haunting and helps you melt even deeper into the experience that is hitting all of your senses. It is an unforgettable experience that you will not find anywhere else. Recommended dishes: Moroccan Salads, Marrocan Pastry, Entrées De Légumes à La Marocaine, Tagine De Ternera Makfoul Kid-friendliness: They are so gracious with kids and every table feels quite cozy and private so you don’t have to worry about intruding on others.

A Culinary Journey to Paradise!  From the moment I stepped through the doors, I was transported to a world of beauty.  The ambience of the restaurant is simply breathtaking. The elegant decor, soft lighting, and stunning views of the surrounding create a sense of tranquility and sophistication.  The service at Dar Yacout is top-notch. The staff are attentive, knowledgeable, and go above and beyond to ensure that every guest feels welcomed and cared for. From the moment we were seated to the final goodbye, we felt like VIPs.  The food, a culinary masterpiece!! Offering a tantalizing array of exotic dishes that are as delicious as they are beautiful. Each dish is thoughtfully crafted with fresh, high-quality ingredients and bursting with flavor. The fusion of flavors and textures is a true delight for the senses.  Speaking of exotic cuisine, Dar Yacout truly excels in this department.  In conclusion, I highly recommend Dar Yacout to anyone looking for a dining experience in Marrakech that is truly out of this world. The ambience, service, food quality, exotic cuisine, and breathtaking beauty all combine to create an unforgettable dining experience like no other.

A night to remember! The menu is a pre-set 4 course affair. You begin with the Moroccan version of salad (about eight different plates of various vegetable tapas ). Next, we had a whole chicken split between the two of us, then lamb and couscous, before ending with dessert. Everything was delicious. (We don't even like lamb and we were pleasantly surprised.) Portions are incredibly large, I would say borderline ludacris for two people. We kept thinking the portions would easily feed a table of four, if not six. It's an incredibly unique experience in a beautiful setting. Just be ready for a preset menu with traditional Moroccan ingredients.
